predecessors.name: Kingdom of the Franks
predecessors.text: the old Burgundian kingdom, central France around Orléans and most of Provence, which Guntram received at the partition of 561 (Francia page)

predecessors.name: Kingdom of the Burgundians
predecessors.text: the old Burgundian kingdom, ended by the Franks in 534

successors.name: Kingdom of the Franks
successors.text: the realm of Neustria and Burgundy under Clovis II and Chlothar III, as Cliopatria draws it to 660

ledger.x: 600: Theuderic and Theudebert beat Chlothar II at Dormelles.
610: Theuderic II loses Alsace, the Saintois, the Thurgau and Champagne to his brother Theudebert II of Austrasia ('In 610, he lost Alsace, the Saintois, the Thurgau, and Champagne to his brother').
About 611: Theuderic routs Theudebert at Toul.
613: Chlothar II takes the whole realm.
639: Clovis II takes Neustria and Burgundy.

wars.name: Wars of Theuderic II and Theudebert II against Chlothar II
wars.outcome: Chlothar II and Fredegund took Paris and beat the two brothers at Laffaux (596); the brothers beat Chlothar at Dormelles (600) and took the land between the Seine and Loire; Chlothar invaded Theuderic's kingdom in 604 (Mayor Berthoald killed at Étampes).

wars.name: War between Theuderic II and Theudebert II
wars.outcome: Theuderic won Alsace, the Saintois, the Thurgau and Champagne in 610, routed Theudebert at Toul (c.

wars.name: Chlothar II's conquest of Burgundy and Austrasia
wars.outcome: After Theuderic II's death the Burgundian and Austrasian nobles deserted Brunhilda and Sigebert II, who were executed; Chlothar II held all three kingdoms and issued the Edict of Paris in 614.

certainty.note: The pages name kings, cities and kingdoms (Burgundy, Austrasia, Neustria, Orléans, Toulouse, Champagne), never a surveyed line; the shapes are Cliopatria's outlines.
